name: VA Cooperative BPH
aliases: Veterans Affairs Cooperative Studies Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia Study Group
question: Do terazosin, finasteride, or their combination improve symptoms and peak urinary flow more than placebo in men with symptomatic BPH?

design.population: 1,229 men aged 45–80 years with symptomatic BPH, AUA symptom score ≥8, peak urinary flow 4–15 mL/s with voided volume ≥125 mL, and postvoid residual <300 mL; no minimum prostate volume.
design.locator: Full text, Methods, Recruitment and eligibility, p 534; Table 1, p 535

verdictNote: Terazosin improved both endpoints; finasteride and its addition to terazosin did not.
takeaway: Over one year, terazosin 10 mg daily improved symptom scores and peak urinary flow versus placebo in men with BPH; finasteride 5 mg daily did not, and adding it to terazosin gave no additional benefit.

reports.label: Primary symptom and flow report
reports.citation: Lepor H, Williford WO, Barry MJ, et al. "The Efficacy of Terazosin, Finasteride, or Both in Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia." *N Engl J Med.* 1996;335(8):533-539. doi:10.1056/NEJM199608223350801
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Methods, Follow-up of Patients, p 534

results.measure: Mean decrease from baseline at 52 weeks, points; observed 52-week cases

effect.p: finasteride vs terazosin <0.001; finasteride vs combination <0.001; terazosin vs combination 1.00; terazosin vs placebo <0.001; combination vs placebo <0.001; finasteride vs placebo 0.63

results.note: Primary pairwise comparisons were finasteride versus terazosin, finasteride versus combination, and terazosin versus combination, with Bonferroni adjustment. Repeated-measures analysis included randomized men with any follow-up data; no numerical between-arm effect estimate or CI was reported.

harms.label: Discontinuation because of adverse effects
harms.note: Adverse-event withdrawal from study treatment; placebo lower than each active arm (P<0.05).

harms.note: Overall four-arm chi-square P=0.05 for impotence and decreased libido; P<0.001 for ejaculatory abnormality.

delivery.locator: Full text, Table 2, p 535; Results, Compliance and Safety, p 535
delivery.note: Mean pill-count compliance ranged from 94% to 98% across arms. Among terazosin and combination recipients, 80% were taking 10 mg at study end.

results.endpoint: Peak flow in men with baseline prostate volume >50 cm3
results.measure: Mean change from baseline at 52 weeks, mL/s; subgroup with baseline and 52-week measurements
results.note: Finasteride versus placebo showed no significant difference in AUA symptom, symptom problem, or BPH impact scores in this subgroup; 17% of study participants had baseline prostate volume >50 cm3.

delivery.label: Terazosin titration and dose reduction
delivery.value: Terazosin or matching placebo at bedtime: 1 mg days 1-3, 2 mg days 4-7, 5 mg days 8-14, then 10 mg from day 15; terazosin could be reduced to 5 mg for an attributed adverse effect. Finasteride or matching placebo was 5 mg nightly.
delivery.note: All arms received matching placebos; protocol allowed blinded dose reduction.
